title: Support Brokerage and Playlet Orchestrator
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Build a lightweight brokerage service (Support Broker) that turns curated runbook steps into composable, RBAC-aware 'playlets' and exposes a safe execution surface for SREs and Support. The broker should validate permissions, run simulated dry-runs, emit standardized telemetry, and surface structured action outputs to Redwood Console. This ticket covers the initial MVP: playlet schema, execution sandbox, permission checks, and integration with runbooks-as-tasks runner.
acceptance_criteria: Playlet schema defined and documented in Confluence with examples for common admin tasks (cache invalidation, model fallback toggle, scale-up request)
Support Broker endpoint implemented that accepts playlet runs and returns structured status with request_id
RBAC enforcement integrated with existing SSO/SAML user roles; unauthorized runs rejected with audit log entry
Dry-run mode runs through a simulated executor and returns predicted side effects without changing production state
Console shows per-playlet telemetry (latency, success/failure, operator, run parameters) and links to originating runbook
End-to-end test coverage for happy path, permission denial, and dry-run behavior
implementation_notes: Design: playlet = small JSON spec with id, inputs, steps (atomic ops), failure_handling policy, rollback hint
Executor: adapter pattern so ops steps map to existing operator utilities or sandboxed shims in staging
Security: all playlet runs must be logged to audit-log with CVE-safe parameter scrubbers; avoid raw secret passthrough
Telemetry: emit structured events to metrics pipeline: playlet.run.start, playlet.run.end, playlet.step.*
Trade-offs: MVP will restrict op surface to a curated whitelist of adapter actions to reduce blast radius; future versions can add parameterized scripts
Performance: expect sub-second validation, median execution latency depends on adapters; include request timeouts configurable per playlet
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal alpha — only SREs in 'support-alpha' group can run playlets in dry-run mode (2 weeks)
Stage 2: broader internal beta — add toggles for 'execute' permission, enable in staging environment (2 weeks)
Stage 3: opt-in GA for platform teams with audit retention enabled and training doc (4 weeks)
Rollback: disable broker service toggle and revoke execute_role binding; all pending runs will be cancelled
